body.statement: For every \(d\geq1\), \(E\geq d+2\), and \(R_{\max}\geq d+2\), there is one fixed compatible choice of the bounded model \(\Theta\), common to all \(r\in\{d+2,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\), such that for every such \(r\) the resulting \(\mathcal B\) contains a nondegenerate finite-dimensional Poisson--Gaussian subclass and two members \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) satisfying \(\beta(\theta_0)\neq\beta(\theta_1)\), \(r^\star(\theta_0)=r^\star(\theta_1)=r\), and \(\mathbb E_{\theta_0}[T_e^pY_e^{\ell}]=\mathbb E_{\theta_1}[T_e^pY_e^{\ell}]\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\) and every \(p,\ell\geq0\) with \(p+\ell<r\).
body.justification: The first breakout order is information-theoretically meaningful, not an artifact of one estimator's search loop.
body.gap: Existing cumulant methods assume a useful nonzero order; they do not construct legal unequal-effect SEMs that match every lower observed mixed moment and become identified exactly at the prescribed order.
body.consumer: The theorem prevents analysts from truncating the moment search below \(r\) while claiming uniform identification over delayed-breakout environments.
body.proof_tex:
We prove the proposed, explicitly quantified claim.  The qualification concerning a compatible fixed experiment is necessary because no lower feasibility relation between the arbitrary moment envelope and the arbitrary calibration gap is present in the frozen assumptions.

Fix \(d,E,R_{\max}\) as in the statement.  Let \(V_e,W_e\) and \(Z\) be mutually independent centered sources.  Give both \(V_e\) and \(W_e\) positive compound-Poisson baseline intensities \(L\) at jumps \(1,\ldots,R_{\max}\), as well as independent nondegenerate Gaussian components.  In environment \(e=j\leq d\), increase the jump-\(j\) intensity of \(V_e\) by \(\eta\) and that of \(W_e\) by \(2\eta\); leave every other intensity at baseline.  Let the invariant outcome source \(Z\) be Gaussian.  Before the order-specific perturbation, define two structural representations by
\[
 \begin{array}{c|ccc|cc}
 &\alpha&\beta&\gamma&\epsilon_{u,e}&\epsilon_{t,e}\\ \hline
 \theta_0^\circ&1&2&1&V_e&W_e\\
 \theta_1^\circ&1&3&-1&W_e&V_e.
 \end{array}                                                   \tag{20}
\]
They have identical observed variables on a common realization, since
\[
 T_e=V_e+W_e,\qquad Y_e=3V_e+2W_e+Z                         \tag{21}
\]
under both rows of (20).  Their calibration contrasts are
\[
 c_k=3\eta(1^k,\ldots,d^k,0,\ldots,0)^\top.                \tag{22}
\]

Fix \(r\in\{d+2,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\), and use the coefficients \(\nu_{rj}\) from (14)--(15).  In the spare environment \(e=d+1\), alter the jump-\(j\) intensity of the treatment source of \(\theta_0^\circ\), namely \(W_{d+1}\), by \(\varepsilon\nu_{rj}\).  Separately, alter the jump-\(j\) intensity of the treatment source of \(\theta_1^\circ\), namely \(V_{d+1}\), by the same amount.  Choose \(\varepsilon\) by (16), so every resulting intensity is positive.  Center each resulting compound-Poisson variable.  Denote the two altered structural parameters by \(\theta_0,\theta_1\).

For every source cumulant order \(s<r\), the alteration is zero by (15), while at order \(r\) it is \(\varepsilon r!\).  Hence all joint cumulants of \((T_e,Y_e)\) of total order below \(r\) equal their unaltered values: this follows directly by multilinearly expanding each joint cumulant in the independent sources in (20).  Those unaltered joint laws agree by (21).  To pass from cumulants to the asserted mixed moments, differentiate the identity between the joint moment generating function and the exponential of its cumulant generating function.  For \(s=p+\ell\), this gives the finite partition formula
\[
 \mathbb E[T_e^pY_e^\ell]
 =\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak P_s}\prod_{D\in\pi}
   \operatorname{cum}\bigl((X_i)_{i\in D}\bigr),             \tag{23}
\]
where \(X_1,\ldots,X_s\) consists of \(p\) copies of \(T_e\) and \(\ell\) copies of \(Y_e\).  Every block in (23) has size at most \(s<r\), so all factors, and therefore the moments, agree under \(\theta_0\) and \(\theta_1\).

The order-specific changes vanish through order \(d+1\), so (22) still determines \(C\) and
\[
 A=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf e_1,\ldots,\mathbf e_d\}.
\]
The latent profile of \(\theta_0\) has coordinate increments \(\eta j^k\), and that of \(\theta_1\) has coordinate increments \(2\eta j^k\); both lie in \(A\) at every order.  At the first nonvanishing spare-coordinate order,
\[
 \begin{array}{c|cc}
 &Q_Ac_r&Q_Am_r\\ \hline
 \theta_0&\varepsilon r!\,\mathbf e_{d+1}&2\varepsilon r!\,\mathbf e_{d+1}\\
 \theta_1&\varepsilon r!\,\mathbf e_{d+1}&3\varepsilon r!\,\mathbf e_{d+1}.
 \end{array}                                                   \tag{24}
\]
Thus both first breakouts equal \(r\), while their effects are \(2\) and \(3\).

The Vandermonde argument proves rank and a positive fixed gap for (22).  Positivity of all jump intensities proves realizability; finite jump support plus Gaussian convolution proves entire moment generating functions.  Since there are finitely many \(r\), choose one coefficient box containing the two rows of (20), one positive calibration gap below \(3\eta\sigma_d(V_d)\), and one finite moment envelope larger than the maximum source moment over all constructions.  These fixed choices make every \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) a member of \(\mathcal B\).  Finally, allowing \(L\) and the Gaussian variances to vary in sufficiently small nontrivial compact intervals preserves positivity, all strict inequalities, (22), and (24).  The resulting subclass is finite-dimensional and nondegenerate, completing the proof.
